title: Why Does the Ocean Have Waves?
mainIdea: Ocean waves are created by different natural forces such as wind, storms, earthquakes, and gravity.

pages.text: The ocean is always moving because waves carry energy through the water.

question.text: What is the topic of the passage?

pages.text: Most waves are created when wind blows across the surface of the ocean.

question.text: What do the waves made by the wind carry?

pages.text: Strong storms can create dangerous waves called storm surges. Earthquakes and volcanoes can create tsunamis.

question.text: What problem can severe weather cause?

pages.text: Earthquakes, landslides, and volcanic eruptions can quickly move large amounts of water and create tsunamis.

question.text: Besides wind and storms, what else can make waves?
options: Only the wind blowing across the surface
Thick storm clouds high above the water

pages.text: The sun and moon create tides through their gravitational pull. Together, these forces keep the ocean moving.

question.text: What happens in the end of the explanation?
options: The ocean stops moving once the wind and the storms go away
Different forces work together to create waves and tides
Tsunamis slowly turn into tides after the moon pulls them in

elements.correct: To move energy across the water
distractors: To carry fish across the ocean
To push ships toward the shore

elements.correct: Storms and earthquakes can create dangerous waves
distractors: Cold water can freeze the waves near the shore
Heavy rain can push the waves back to the shore

elements.correct: Wind, storms, earthquakes, and gravity form waves
distractors: Rain, clouds, snow, and moonlight form waves
Boats, birds, and fishing nets form waves

elements.correct: The ocean remains in constant motion
distractors: The ocean freezes when the tide goes out
The ocean grows calm after every storm
